title: italys edison trims 2026 guidance again over iran war weak hydro power 2026 07 30
text:
MILAN, July 30 (Reuters) - Italian utility Edison (EDNn.MI)
, opens new tab
 on Thursday cut its full-year earnings guidance for the second time this year as first-half results were hit by disruptions to Qatari gas supplies and weak hydroelectric generation.
Edison, ​one of QatarEnergy's main gas customers in Europe, now expects earnings before interest, taxes, ​depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of €1.1-1.2 billion this year, from a previous guidance of €1.2-1.4 ⁠billion.
Edison had first trimmed its EBITDA guidance when it released first-quarter results in May.
First-half EBITDA fell ​to €607 million ($695 million) from €736 million a year earlier, the company said on Thursday.
The decline ​was mainly due to a 27% drop in hydroelectric generation, but was also driven by lower volumes of gas received from Qatar and voluntary measures taken to support vulnerable retail customers ​in Italy, Edison said.
Edison, a unit of French energy group EDF, has ​a long-term contract with QatarEnergy for 6.4 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas per year, equivalent to ‌10% ⁠of Italy's annual gas consumption.
The U.S. war against Iran forced QatarEnergy to shut liquefaction trains, declare force majeure on deliveries and suspend exports.
Renewed Iranian attacks this month on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have further clouded prospects for a ​return to pre-conflict energy ​flows.
Under a ⁠force majeure notice, QatarEnergy said it would not deliver 24 liquefied natural gas (LNG) cargoes to Edison between April and the ​end of September.
Edison has so far replaced 17 cargoes, ​equivalent to ⁠about 1.6 bcm of gas, as it pledged to meet commitments to customers.
Despite lower earnings, Edison said it increased investments by 13% in the first half, pushing ⁠ahead ​with renewable energy projects.
The group reported a ​net credit position of €254 million at the end of June, up from €219 million at the end of ​last year.
($1 = 0.8732 euros)
